title: Veronica Moran
text:
Veronica Moran holds a B.S. in Biology and a minor in Environmental Science from California State University, Monterey Bay. As an undergraduate, she assessed the results of a long-term vegetation monitoring project at Fort Ord National Monument, using geostatistical modeling to evaluate goat grazing as a land management practice. Her capstone examined large woody debris as a restoration strategy in the Carmel River following the removal of San Clemente Dam, using benthic macroinvertebrate bioassessments to evaluate stream ecological health.
At Santa Barbara Channelkeeper, an environmental nonprofit, Veronica contributed to long-term marine and coastal monitoring, including vessel-based Marine Protected Area Watch surveys, tar ball baseline surveys, and harmful algal bloom monitoring. She developed geospatial tools to improve data collection, management, and visualization. Her work extended to managing a community engagement program focused on marine debris removal and supporting environmental education and outreach on watersheds, water quality, and marine conservation.
Building on these experiences, Veronica is pursuing a Master of Environmental Data Science at UCSB. She aims to apply data science to inform solutions to environmental challenges and is particularly interested in water quality, coastal resilience, and sustainable resource management.
